anomalies.observed: Both M12 CAN connectors J10 ("CAN Interface B") and J11 ("CAN Interface A") have pins connected to the same four CAN bus nets: /NET0054 (CANH of U19), /NET0083 (CANL of U19), /NET0088 (CANH of U20), and /NET0040 (CANL of U20).
anomalies.expected: Each M12 connector should carry only its own isolated CAN bus. J10 should connect to one bus (e.g., U20) and J11 to the other (e.g., U19), keeping the two isolated CAN buses separate.

evidence.quote: two isolated CAN buses (CAN0, CAN1), each driven by its own MCP2515 SPI CAN controller ... broken out on M12 circular connectors J2 ("CAN Interface A") and J13 ("CAN Interface B").

anomalies.impact: The two isolated CAN buses are shorted together at the connectors, defeating isolation and causing bus contention or communication failure.

anomalies.observed: The 120R termination resistors R4 and R44 are connected to the wrong CANH nets via SW4. R4 is between /NET0040 (CANL of U20) and SW4.1; R44 is between /NET0083 (CANL of U19) and SW4.2. SW4.3 is /NET0054 (CANH of U19) and SW4.4 is /NET0088 (CANH of U20).
anomalies.expected: Each 120R termination resistor should connect between the CANH and CANL of the same bus. R4 should terminate U20 (between /NET0088 and /NET0040) and R44 should terminate U19 (between /NET0054 and /NET0083).
anomalies.impact: The CAN termination is cross-connected between the two buses, so enabling termination can short the buses together or provide incorrect termination, causing communication errors.

parsed.summary: The design files contain two related CAN wiring anomalies: both M12 CAN connectors are wired in parallel to both isolated CAN buses, and the 120R termination resistors are cross-connected between the two buses. These deviations would short the isolated CAN buses together and prevent proper operation.
